title: Close encounter
caption: The interacting galaxies IRAS 06076-2139, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: IRAS 06076-2139 · constellation Lepus · about 500 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows IRAS 06076-2139, an unusual object in the constellation Lepus (The Hare), 500 million light-years away. What might pass for a single galaxy is in fact two separate galaxies racing past each other.

The pair are moving at about 2 million kilometers per hour. That speed is most likely too high for them to settle into one merged galaxy, so the encounter will probably end with the two going their own ways rather than combining.

The meeting will still leave its mark. The galaxies are only about 20 000 light-years apart, close enough that each will pull on the other through gravity as they pass. That tug is expected to reshape their structures on a grand scale. Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 and its Advanced Camera for Surveys both contributed observations of the pair, which ESA/Hubble describes as rushing past each other.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.27 x 2.67 arcminutes) and distance (500 million light years), the frame spans roughly 476,000 × 388,000 light-years. Its light set out about 500 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3 observed through visible-light filters at 435 nm and 814 nm and a near-infrared filter at 1.545 μm. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: One of the filters records near-infrared light, which is invisible to the eye.
